intent: I finally have about 120 dollars saved for my first mechanical keyboard after years on a mushy laptop-style board. I split my time between office writing all day and playing shooters at night, and I'm stuck between a cheaper hot-swappable board that leaves money for nicer switches later, or blowing the whole budget on a well-known prebuilt. I honestly don't even know whether linear or tactile switches suit someone like me, or what people who bought each option ended up regretting. What actually matters at this price, and what would you put in the cart if you were me?
author_notes: Deep-tier task v1 — see configs/deep_topics/V1_TASK_DESIGN_GRID.md §2 for spec.
intent_v1_legacy: I've spent an embarrassing amount of money chasing sleep lately and I'm starting to suspect most of it is snake oil. The 10mg melatonin gummies, the watch that claims to track my sleep stages, blue-light glasses, magnesium glycinate, and now a weighted blanket, everything promises the same fix. Before I buy anything else, can you tell me which of these actually work? I've heard tiny melatonin doses might beat big ones, which makes me distrust everything. And if the honest answer is 'skip the products', I'd take a short list of habits that genuinely help instead.

tri_source.angle: First mechanical board on a fixed $120: cheap hot-swap plus better switches later vs. one well-known prebuilt, split gaming/typing use
